title: Word, Numerical and General Analogy
shortDescription: Find the relationship in a given pair and apply it to another — words, numbers and letters.
genZNote: Analogy is 'same relationship, new pair'. Say the relationship out loud as a sentence before you choose.

sections.heading: Numerical and Letter Analogy
bullets: Operations on both terms: (a, b) → a² + b, a × b, a + b etc.
Letter analogy: use alphabet positions; reverse alphabet pairs sum to 27 (A–Z, B–Y).

sections.heading: General Analogy
sections.body: Includes profession–tool, country–capital (India : New Delhi), author–book, units (Length : Metre), symbols and function pairs. Always check the direction of the relationship (A : B vs B : A) and the grammatical type.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Analogy questions test whether you can identify the exact relationship between a pair and carry it to a new pair.
keyFacts: State the relationship as a sentence.

commonTraps: Do not pick a related but not identical relationship.
mustRemember: A : B :: C : ? means same relationship.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
